newsitem.title: GERMANY: Traub says Index can pursue takeover talks.
newsitem.headline: Traub says Index can pursue takeover talks.

text.p: Bankrupt German machine tool-maker Traub AG said on Thursday its administrator was due to discuss a takeover offer by the Esslingen-based Index-Werke GmbH after the approach had received the approval of creditor banks.
Agreement on an offer will be sought in discussions to start in the coming days so that any deal can go ahead in early March, Traub said in a statement.
A rival proposal by machine-manufacturer Gildemeister AG, which would have saved more jobs at Traub's main plant in Reichenbach, had been rejected by the banks, a Traub spokesman said.
Traub currently has some 750 workers, of whom Index is expected to keep 450. Both Traub and Index are leading manufacturers of motorised lathes.
Index last year increased its turnover by 10 percent to 440 million marks ($261 million), with some 1,550 staff.
Traub said on Tuesday that bankruptcy proceedings had been initiated following the failure of efforts to scale back debt with creditors.
